name: glucose-biomodel-do
title: Glucose BioModel Digital Objects — Uberon Organ Annotation
question:
Can glucose-regulation BioModels be annotated with HRA Uberon organ terms
(via transparent synonym matching) and inverted into an organ->models index?

study_card.goal: Search BioModels for 'glucose regulation', annotate each hit with HRA reference-organ synonyms, and build the organ(Uberon)->model-ids index.
study_card.mechanism: BiomodelDOCatalogStep.update -> build_biomodel_do_catalog(query, max_results) = search_biomodels_detailed + build_organ_index(HRA reference organs) + annotate_biomodel (synonym-match) -> biomodel_dos + organ_to_models -> RAMEmitter.
study_card.expected_result: At least one glucose-regulation BioModel maps to at least one HRA organ (pancreas is expected to dominate given insulin/glucagon/beta-cell synonyms).
study_card.main_expert_question: Is synonym-based annotation (vs a real ontology/NLP classifier) precise enough to trust the organ->models index for downstream multiscale coupling?

biological_summary:
Glucose homeostasis is a liver-pancreas circuit: pancreatic beta cells
sense blood glucose and secrete insulin/glucagon, which the liver reads to
switch between glycogen synthesis and glycogenolysis/gluconeogenesis.
A "biomodel DO" (digital object) makes that anatomical grounding explicit
by tagging each BioModels SBML entry with the HRA reference organ(s) its
name/synonyms implicate, so a downstream multiscale composite can ask
"which glucose models actually touch the pancreas vs the liver" instead
of treating the whole search-result set as anatomically undifferentiated.

report.title: Glucose BioModel DOs — 5/25 models organ-tagged (4 pancreas, 1 liver)
report.objective:
Can glucose-regulation BioModels be annotated with HRA Uberon organ
terms (via transparent synonym matching) and inverted into an
organ->models index?
report.conclusion:
A live run of `build_biomodel_do_catalog("glucose regulation", 25)`
built 25 biomodel DOs (one per search hit) against the live 81-organ
HRA reference-organ set; 5/25 (20%) matched >=1 organ synonym in the
model name. The organ->models index has 2 organs: pancreas
(UBERON:0001264, 4 models — MODEL2001080002 Topp beta-cell-mass,
MODEL1112110004 Silber intravenous-glucose, BIOMD0000000382 Sturis
ultradian-oscillation, BIOMD0000000372 Tolic insulin-glucose-feedback)
and liver (UBERON:0002107, 1 model — BIOMD0000000633 Bulik2016 hepatic
glucose metabolism), confirming pancreas dominates as expected
(insulin/glucagon/beta-cell synonyms) while liver also surfaces via the
"hepatic" synonym.
report.caveat:
Synonym matching only scans the model *name*, not its full
description/annotations, so the 80% unmatched rate (20/25) likely
undercounts real anatomical relevance — many unmatched titles (e.g.
generic "glucose-insulin model" variants) plausibly implicate
pancreas/liver too but don't say so in the name string. This is exactly
the study's main expert question: precision here trades off against
recall, and downstream multiscale coupling should treat
`organ_to_models` as a high-precision/low-recall starting index, not a
complete one.

readouts: count of distinct organs (Uberon CURIEs) with >=1 mapped model

embed_visualizations.description: Time-course overlay for BIOMD0000000633 (Bulik2016 hepatic glucose metabolism), this catalog's one liver-tagged model — COPASI (solid) vs Tellurium (dashed), from the committed full-corpus dataset (mean nRMSE 1.61e-07, 'good').

findings.statement:
Synonym-based organ tagging matched 5/25 (20%) glucose-regulation
BioModels to an HRA organ, correctly concentrating on pancreas (4
models -- Topp beta-cell-mass, Silber IV-glucose, Sturis and Tolic
insulin-glucose oscillators) and liver (1 model, Bulik2016 hepatic
glucose metabolism) -- exactly the two organs glucose-homeostasis
biology predicts (insulin/glucagon secretion + hepatic glucose
buffering), confirming the synonym-match mechanism assigns organs
correctly when it fires.

evidence.summary: organ_to_models has 2 organs from 25 search hits: pancreas (UBERON:0001264, 4 models), liver (UBERON:0002107, 1 model); 5/25 (20%) tagged overall.

regression_compatibility.basis: The baseline biomodel-DO catalog build (25-result query x 81-organ HRA reference set) completed without error.

biological_validation.basis: The organ_to_models index correctly concentrates on pancreas (4 models) and liver (1 model) -- precisely the two organs glucose-homeostasis biology implicates -- confirming the synonym-match mechanism works, though only on the 20% of titles containing a matching organ synonym (name-only, recall-limited).

explanatory_gain.basis: F-01 shows precision (organ assignment matches expected biology) is real, but the 80% unmatched rate is the study's central caveat: recall trades off against precision when scanning only model names.

limitations: Synonym matching scans only the model name, not full description/annotations, so the 80% unmatched rate (20/25) likely undercounts real anatomical relevance.
Sample is a single 25-result search query, not the full BioModels corpus (see corpus-coverage for the full-catalog organ-tagging yield, 82/1,096).

resolved_uncertainties: Pancreas and liver dominate the organ->models index exactly as glucose-homeostasis biology predicts, validating the synonym-match mechanism's precision.
remaining_uncertainties: Is name-only synonym matching precise enough to trust for downstream multiscale coupling, or does it need SBML MIRIAM-annotation-based tagging to raise recall?
